summary: Norway Bluff's 24-ft steel tower (Piscataquis Co., ME) came down in May 2012 for the MSCommNet radio project, was restored by volunteers and dedicated at the Ashland Logging Museum on 7 July 2013.

facts.design: 24-foot steel lookout tower with a wood cab, which was reconditioned for the move
facts.status_note: Listed as standing at the Ashland Logging Museum grounds (FFLA); the original Norway Bluff site is listed as gone
facts.agency: Maine Forestry District (per Forest Lookouts); dismantled by the Maine Forest Service in 2012

events.note: The 1914 Forest Commissioner's report says the 24-foot steel tower was built during the previous summer; the exact build year is not stated
Watchman's camp built on the mountainside; telephone line linked the lookout man to Oxbow Plantation
Taken off the mountain on 7 May 2012 as part of the MSCommNet radio project
Moved to the Ashland Logging Museum on 13 June 2012
Carpentry repairs under way at the museum site in early October 2012
Volunteers and Ashland Boy Scout Troop 179 put in well over 600 hours on the cab, painted frame and reassembly
Dedication ceremony held at the museum on 7 July 2013

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The County article says the tower was moved from Norway Bluff in May 2012. The 2012 Maine chapter report says it came off the mountain on 7 May 2012 and reached the museum on 13 June 2012. The story gives both steps.
The Forest Lookouts page announced the dedication as a future event. The 2013 Maine chapter report confirms it was held on 7 July 2013.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced from the Forest Lookouts page, the 2012 and 2013 Maine chapter reports, the 2012 historians report and a 2013 dedication notice. Current condition and public access are not confirmed. The FFLA list says standing. A Visit Aroostook search snippet mentions climbing the tower, but the page itself does not, so it was not used. Staffing: a watchman's camp existed in 1914; no names or later staffing found. The record's 2012 'relocated' event could take the 7 May 2012 removal date as well. The record's 2012 'restored' note describes a carpentry step, not completed restoration; the 2013 event covers the finish. No photos added; a Maine chapter Facebook post and Ashland Logging Museum pages were seen only as search snippets.
